item.title: Putin thanks Orbán for EU veto, amid Iran-war ‘nightmare’ for Kyiv
item.description: Russian president Vladimir Putin phoned his ally, Hungarian prime minister Viktor Orbán, on Tuesday to “commend” his "principled" and "sovereign" Ukraine foreign policy, according to a Kremlin readout.

item.title: What the 2022 energy crisis taught us about inflation — and why it matters now with Iran
item.description: The European Central Bank itself has repeatedly said over the years that its policies are ineffective when dealing with energy shocks.

item.title: Listen: Should Europeans fear a new energy crisis with the blockade of the Strait of Hormuz?
item.description: Iran is now blocking the Strait of Hormuz, through which one in five barrels of oil and a quarter of the world’s liquefied natural gas transit. As oil and gas prices rise, should Europeans be worried about a new energy crisis?

item.title: How the EU is building a dystopian, surveillance-driven, deportation machine
item.description: Like much recent EU migration legislation, the proposal was presented without a comprehensive fundamental rights impact assessment. Sixteen UN experts have already raised concerns about its compatibility with international law. Yet EU institutions are rushing the file through the legislative process.

item.title: EU Commission backs Spain after Trump’s Iran war trade threat to Sánchez
item.description: The European Commission's remarks follow the threat by Donald Trump to halt all trade with Spain, following PM Pedro Sánchez denial of the use of military bases in the peninsula for further attacks against Iran.

item.title: Iran war could mean shortages of Patriot defence missiles for Ukraine
item.description: Ukraine has backed US action against Iran, seeking favour with Donald Trump and strategic gains against Russia, despite risks of reduced US support and Patriot shortages. Meanwhile, Emmanuel Macron has expanded France’s nuclear umbrella to Europe, including Poland — while disputes intensify over Ukraine’s Druzhba pipeline shutdown.

item.title: Deportations, visas and police powers on EU interior ministers’ agenda
item.description: A senior EU diplomat told reporters that ministers will focus on ways to compel people to return home voluntarily, amid wider migration talks on working with Lebanon and Libya.

item.title: When a European airline chooses to delay, they still must pay, ECJ rules
item.description: If a European airline chooses to delay a flight due to extraordinary circumstances, causing later flights to be delayed, it must compensate the subsequent passengers, according to a new European Court of Justice ruling on Wednesday.

item.title: Iran war shifts EU attention from ‘extreme’ Israeli actions in Gaza
item.description: The EU Parliament should — at the least — hold a plenary debate on Gaza to hold Israel to account despite the Iran crisis, leftwing, Green, and liberal groups told press in Brussels on Wednesday.

item.title: EU inches towards migration and investment pact with Senegal
item.description: Migration control is at the heart of a planned 'strategic partnership' between the EU and Senegal.
